rules.name: Bombardment
rules.description: Due to British tactical doctrine which relied on extensive Preparatory Bombardment British and Commonwealth roll 2 dice for each target unit, choosing the best die roll as a result.

rules.name: Artillery Support
rules.description: British platoons may include one free Artillery Forward Observer. Platoons may purchase another Artillery Forward Observer if desired.

rules.name: National Characteristic
rules.description:
A British army may choose one of the following rules:
•	Up and at ‘em: all regular and veteran units may assault without an order test.
•	Blood Curdling Charge: when all regular and veteran units assault, the enemy unit cannot react.
•	Tough as Boots: all regular and veteran units may assault with one extra die for every three figures.
•	Rapid Fire: all regular and veteran units fire with one extra die for every three figures.
•	Vengeance: all regular and veteran units receive one free order test whenever enemy units are within 12”. For this test roll 1D6. On a roll of 4+ a pin is removed. Then roll for a regular order test to see if the unit can act. Roll even if the unit no longer has any pins; just use the standard morale.

rules.name: Artillery Command Vehicle
rules.description: If field artillery and Centaur platoons (i.e. not anti-tank platoons), the command vehicle may be upgraded to a spotter for +40pts. This allows the other vehicles in the platoon to use the command vehicle's line of sight for indirect fire each turn. The command vehicle may not fire any turrent mounted weapons the same turn as being used as a spotter.

rules.name: Troop Integrity
rules.description: Aside from the command vehice, all other vehicles in the platoon (not including transports and tows) must be of the same type.

rules.name: Balaklavering
rules.description: Harking back to their cavalry ancestry, British tanks in the early war period were prone to charge at top speed towards enemy formations. Whilst presenting quite a spectacle it often resulted in disastrous losses against static anti-tank defences. It was not restricted to the cruisers either, with units of ponderous Matildas also joining in. All tanks in this selector (including Inexperienced tanks) can use the ‘Up and At ’Em’ national characteristic.

rules.name: Firing on the move
rules.description: A common dilemma for tank crews was whether to fire on the move or when halted. Moving and firing might be less accurate but it made the firing tank a more difficult target. Firing while stationary might bring better accuracy but it also made the firer an easier target. For the British, who sought maximum mobility in their tank forces, the former was preferable. Any tank or armoured car from this selector may fire at any enemy vehicle when performing a Run move with a to hit modifier of -3.

rules.name: Cool Heads
rules.description: During 1942, the Commonwealth armoured brigades took some terrible beatings from Axis anti-tank fire. Yet despite the losses they stuck to their missions and gave as good as they got. When firing, Commonwealth tanks ignore the die roll modifier for pin markers.

rules.name: Must be Mobile
rules.description: There must be enough transport vehicles in the platoon for every soldier to ride

rules.name: Been there, done that
rules.description: All British and Commonwealth forces must be Veteran if the option is aviable

rules.name: Baptism of Fire
rules.description: No British and Commonwealth forces can be Veteran

rules.name: Resolute
rules.description: British infantry were resolute in defence. If a British infantry or artillery unit that was treated as in cover when the enemy fired at it suffers enough casualities to cause a Morale check, the unit benefits from a +1 Morale modifier for the check

rules.name: Sticky
rules.description: British infantry and artillery tended to get separeted from advancing armour. British infantry and artillery units must always take an Order test when given an advance or run order, even if the unit is not pinned.

sharedRules.name: 75MM AT-gun
sharedRules.description: HE: Instead of causing D2 HE hits, an HE shell causes D6 hits.

sharedRules.name: Fire & Manoeuvre
sharedRules.description: The unit do not suffer the -1 to hit penality when making advance orders.

sharedRules.name: Scary Blighters
sharedRules.description: Any enemy unit fighting Ghurkas in close combat will halve its total number of attacks against the Ghurkas (rounding up).

sharedRules.name: 'Who dares win'!
sharedRules.description: To represent their special training and motivation, SAS units have the fanatics special rule.

sharedRules.name: LZ Signals
sharedRules.description: If you deploy at least one unit of Pathfinders on the table before the game states (i.e. the Pathfinders are not in the first wave or in reserve), then any friendly paratroopers and glider units in reserve may re-roll failed Order tests to come onto the table

sharedRules.name: Discipline
sharedRules.description: Gurads do not benefit from the National Characteristic army special rule; instead they may re-roll order tests. They must accept the second result. A re-roll may not be taken if a FUBAR result is rolled.

sharedRules.name: 'Faugh a Ballagh!' (Clear the way!)
sharedRules.description: Irish units do not benefit from the National Characteristic you have chosen for the rest of your army; they instead use the Vegance national characteristic.

sharedRules.name: Bagpiper
sharedRules.description: The bagpiper effectively makes the platoon a Highland platoon. As long as the bagpiper is alive, Regular and Veteran Infantry sections in this platoon may reroll failed morale checks. FUBAR rolls cannot be rerolled.

sharedRules.name: Armoured OP
sharedRules.description: An Armoured OP Vehicle is a transport vehicle, but may only transport an Artillery Forward Observer team of up to three models. Provided the Armoured OP vehicle has not yet been given an order, an embarked Artillery Forward Observer team can be given a Fire order to allow them to call in their artillery mission using the line of sight of the vehicle. As soon as an embarked Artillery Forward Observer Team is given the Fire order, pull another order die and give the vehicle a Down order. If the vehicle has already been given an order die this turn, the Artillery Forward Observer Team is assumed to be busy executing that order and may not call in their artillery mission on that turn.

sharedRules.name: M3 Stuart Forward Facing Hull Mounted LMG
sharedRules.description: Note that these .30 cal machine guns are treated as LMGs rather than MMGs to represent the awkwardness of this weapon layout. In addition, these weapons must always be fired against the same target as the vehicle hull mounted MMG.

sharedRules.name: Little John Adaptor
sharedRules.description: + 1 armour penetration. Cannot fire HE while fitted. If you roll a 1 (before modification) when you are rolling to hit then it has broken. The main weapon cannot be fired again until the crew repair it. Whenever you give an order to the tank again, you can give it a Down order to represent the repairs. When you do this, the vehicle does not move and counts as open-topped for the rest of the turn, but the main gun becomes fully operational again. Remember it is now  a normal light AT-gun.

sharedRules.name: AT Rounds
sharedRules.description: The light howitzer may be fired as a light anti-tank gun.

sharedRules.name: Cullin Hedgerow Cutter
sharedRules.description: Any tank that has the option of adding a Culin hedgerow cutter may do so for +10 points per model. A tank so equipped may move at advance rate through any bocage or edgerow or comparable obstacle that is otherwise rated impassable to vehicles. As it does so it automaticaly creates a gap passable to any tracked vehicles moving at advance rate.

rules.name: Intelligence
rules.description: Once per game, at the beginning of any turn before the first die is drawn from the dice bag. Roll a D6 and apply modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the player activating the Intelligence Officer may choose a die from the bag for the first activation. If both players attempt to activate this ability simultaneously, each must roll 1D6. The higher score wins and immediately uses this ability, but the losing player may attempt to use his ability on another turn instead.

rules.name: Inspiring Presence
rules.description: Upon receiving his order dice (except for Down), a chaplain may select one friendly unit within 6" and roll a D6, applying the following modifiers: Inexperienced -1, Veteran +1. On a 4+, the chaplain may remove 1 pin from the selected unit.

rules.name: Non Combatant
rules.description: The chaplain is there to support the soldiers, not win battles. A chaplain unit cannot be used to claim or contest objectives.

rules.name: Self-defence only
rules.description: Clergymen are not soldiers and will not take part in hostile actions - they cannot fire any weapon, nor assault enemy units. If your chaplain is equipped with a pistol, it can only be used in close quarters if the enemy assaults him (including firing it at the assaulting enemies as a reaction, if applicable).

rules.name: Gun assembly
rules.description: To simulate the fact that the gun was actually transported disassembled, when the gun is unlimbered the artillery unit suffers a pin. When the gun is limbered, the mule team (and consequently the transported artillery unit) suffers a pin.

rules.name: Stubborn (Mule)
rules.description: When taking an order test and doubles are rolled, the mules become stubborn and refuse to cooperate even if the order test was passed. Place the order dice to Down and add 1 pin marker to th eteam. This rule does not apply if Fubar is rolled.

rules.name: Extra Selection
rules.description: you may take up to three Motorcycle and Sidecars as one selection in each reinforced platoon. A maximum of one light mortar and one anti-tank rifle may be taken in each reinforced platoon.

rules.name: Questionable Firing Platform
rules.description: The sidecar is purely a transportation option for a light mortar or VB launcher, attempting to fire from inside the sidecar would result in a one shot weapon. Light mortars and VB launchers need to be removed from the sidecar to fire and so can only be operated with a Fire order.
